title: Intrinsic realization of the theta coefficient square without orientation
statement: Fix a finite setting P, 1 ≤ m ≤ P.level and smooth separated finite-type f:X→Y of pure dimension d between separated finite-type schemes over P.field.k. For intrinsic finite-Tor constructible K, let K_m be its intrinsic reduction. For every etale presentation J,e of inverse-realized K and Jprime,eprime of inverse-realized K_m, red_X(finitePurityTheta_P(f,K,J,e)) followed by finiteReductionExceptionalComparison equals finiteReductionTensorOmegaComparison followed by finitePurityTheta_Q(f,K_m,Jprime,eprime). This is the tensor adjunction factor alone, with no diagonal orientation or purity map. The definitions used here are recorded in [def-pur-finite-reduction-tensor-factors], [def-pur-finite-reduction-comparisons].

proof.text: Take bounded flat etale models and reduce termwise; the Tor interval is preserved. Apply finite_adjoint_mate_tensor to the actual coefficient quotient. Its unit normalization and source-order symmetry give the ordinary smoothPurityEtaleTheta square.

Transport the ordinary square through site tensor and pullback comparisons and scalarPresentation. The latter is the scalar-unit-normalized mate of the sectionwise restriction square. Naturality in the two presentation isomorphisms gives exactly finiteReductionTensorOmegaComparison; its omega factor is the presented exceptional-unit counit mate omegaMap.

The transported target coefficient map has reduced counit as transpose. Uniqueness in existsUnique_finiteReductionExceptionalComparison identifies it with the specified intrinsic exceptional map. The site and realization triangle identities cancel the conjugating units and counits. Presentation naturality gives the equality for arbitrary J,e,Jprime,eprime.
